full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J : This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Sessions Case No. 863 of 2010 arising out of CR Case No. 998 of 2009 (Double Mooring Zone) under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act (amended), 1881 now pending in the Court of the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. Ultimately the case record was transmitted to the Court of the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong for trial, who after hearing both the parties by order dated 12-8-2012 framed charge against the accused-petitioner and another under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. 

 6. Mr Mohammad Jahedul Alain Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner submits that the cause of action for prosecution will arise under clause (c) of the proviso of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act on the failure of the accused to pay the amount within 30 days of the receipt of the notice of the complainant and it is on record that the complainant issued legal notice to the accused-petitioner on 29-6-2009 and filed the case on 17-9-2009 although the petition of compliant was required to be filed within one month from 29-6-2009 in compliance with clause (b) of section 141 of the Act which having not been done by the complainant and, as such, the case is plainly barred by section 141(b) of the Negotiable Instrument Act. The learned Advocate further submits that as per mandatory provision of section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act there are 3 alternative ways for serving notice upon the accused, that is : a) by delivering it to the person on whom it is to be served, or (b) by sending it by registered post with acknowledgement due to that person at his usual and last known place of abode or business in Bangladesh; or (c) by publication in a Daily Bangla national newspaper having wide circulation but in this case the complaint published Legal Notice through the local newspaper namely "Dainik Suprovat Bangladesh" which is not a wide circulated Daily Bangla national newspaper and as such, the impugned proceeding is liable to be quashed. Mr Chowdhury to fortify his argument has relied on a unreported judgment of this Court dated 3-7-2014 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 29 111 of 2013. 

 7. Mr Aminul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the complainant-opposite party No. 2 in the course of his argument after placing the petition of complaint as well as counter-affidavit submits that in the present case, the cause of action arose on 28-8-2009 and the petition of complaint was filed on 17-9-2009, that is, well within one month from 28-8-2009. He further submits that the complainant-opposite party published Legal Notice through the daily national newspaper namely Dainik Suprovat Bangladesh" which is a wide circulated Bangla national newspaper and the complainant filed the case after exhausting all the legal formalities but the accused-petitioner with illegal motive to hang the process of realization of cheque's money filed this application under section 561A CrPC at the belated stage without any legal basis. Finally, Mr Islam relying on a decision reported in 13 MLR (AD) 103 = 1=1 BLC (AD) 26 submits that in this case trial has already been started and PW-1 was examined and as such, there no valid ground for quashing the proceeding under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. 

 (b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice, in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid, and 

 (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment for the said amount of money to the payee or as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of the said notice. 

 141. Cognizance of offences—Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898)—(a) no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under section 138 expect upon a complaint, in writing, made by the payee or, as the case may be, the holder in due course of the cheque; (b) such complaint is made within one month of the date on which the cause of action arises under clause (c) of the proviso to section 138; (c) no court inferior to that of a Court of Sessions shall try any offence punishable under section 138. 

 13. The main ground on which the accused petitioner has pressed this Rule that the compliant in the present case not having been made in terms of clause (b) of section 141 i.e. the complaint having not been filed within one month of the date on which the cause of action arose under clause (b) of the proviso to section 138, the taking of cognizance was illegal and, therefore, the proceeding is liable to be quashed. 

 14. It appears from the petition of complaint. that the accused-petitioner took loan amounting to Taka 7,00,000 (seven lac) from accused-petitioner for the purpose of his business and thereafter, the accused-petitioner to repay the loan amount issued a cheque of Taka 7,00,000 (seven lac), vide cheque No. 8688698 dated 25-6-2009 in favour of the complainant opposite party, who deposited the said cheque on 28-6-2009 in his account at Pubali Bank Ltd. and the same was dishonoured on the same date with the remark that fund insufficient and thereafter, the complainant-opposite party sent a legal notice through his learned lawyer to the accused-petitioner on 29-6-2009 asking to pay the cheque's amount although the accused-petitioner on various pretext did not receive the said notice and thereafter, the complainant-opposite party published the said legal notice through "Dainik Suprovat Bangladesh" on 27-7-2009 asking to pay the cheque's amount within 30 days and the accused petitioner failed to pay the cheque's amount of money and thereafter, the complainant filed the case on 17-9-2009, that is, well within the period of one month from 27-8-2009 in compliance with clause (b) of section 141 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. Therefore, the plea as canvassed by the learned Advocate for accused-petitioner that the petition of compliant was not filed within one month from the cause of action in compliance with clause (b) of section 141 of the Act and hence, the proceeding is liable to be quashed does not find any leg to stand up. 

 15. Now, to meet the second branch of argument that the notice was not published in well circulated daily national newspaper as per mandatory provision of section 138(c) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, and as such , the continuation of the proceeding is abuse of the process of the Court, the same is liable to be quashed, we have carefully examined the provision of section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act to the best of our ability and find the provision with regard to serve notice in a well circulated Bangla national newspaper is merely directory in nature and not mandatory since there is no legal mandate or consequence to stop or dismiss the case or the accused shall stand discharged from the case proceeding, if notice is not served through a Bangla national newspaper having wide circulation. Moreover, Mr Aminul Islam the learned Advocate for the complainant-opposite party argues with force that the complainant-opposite party published his legal notice "Dainik Suprovat Bangladesh" which is a wide circulated daily Bangla national newspaper. The very correctness of fact whether "Dainik Suprovat Bangladesh" is a wide circulated daily Bangla national newspaper or not can only be adjudicated at the trial. 

 16. On a reading of the petition of complaint it is difficult to hold that there is any legal bar or the continuation of the impugned proceeding will amount to an abuse of the process of the Court. Under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act an offence is committed if a cheque is dishonoured and if payment is not made within 30 days after receipt of a legal notice and in this case it is on record that the complainant-opposite party published the said legal notice through "Dainik Suprovat Bangladesh" on 27-7-2009 asking to pay the cheque's amount within 30 days but the accused-petitioner failed to pay the cheque's amount and thereafter, the complainant filed the case on 17-9-2009, that is, well within the period of one month from 27-8-2009 in compliance with clause (b) of section 141 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. Further, the proposition of law is by now well settled that on the basis of the defence plea or materials, the criminal proceedings should not be stifled before trial, when there is a prima-facie case for going to the trial. 

 17. Taking into consideration of all these aspects of the case as well as principle of law, we are of the view that the petition of complaint undoubtedly discloses that the accused-petitioner is liable for the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, the question of quashing the proceeding does not arise at all. 

 18. Here it may further be mentioned that the unreported judgment of this Court relied upon by the petitioner has also no manner of application in the facts and circumstance of the case as the facts of the instant case are quite distinguishable from the facts of the said case. 

 20. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. Since this petty case has been dragging for over a period of 8 years the trial Court concerned is directed to proceed with the case expeditiously in accordance with law without giving any adjournment to the parties.
